post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations.physical_scope: An equation-based adoption for a specified smooth classical matter model on the selected oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold. The matter current and stress are supplied by that model. This postulate does not assume a matter action, assert existence of solutions, include singular sources or establish empirical validity.

post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations:
## Postulate

Let $M$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with metric $g$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ and the curvature convention of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Take a smooth real
two-form $F$ and smooth current vector $j$ on $U$, with
$dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ under the adopted convention of
[[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]]. A chosen smooth matter model supplies a smooth
symmetric covariant tensor $T^m_{ab}$ on $U$ and the current $j$; this postulate
does not assert that arbitrary independently prescribed $T^m$ and $j$ arise
from a matter model.

Define the Einstein tensor by $G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
-\tfrac12 Rg_{ab}$, using the curvature contractions of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], and define the smooth-field electromagnetic
stress tensor by

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

For constant cosmological parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and
$\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, adopt the additional equation-based gravitational
field law

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E\left(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}\right).$$

Here $c>0$, $G_N>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ have the SI roles and units fixed in
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]; in length coordinates, $G_{ab}$ and
$\Lambda g_{ab}$ have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ and $T^m$
have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $\kappa_E$ has units
$\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. The source-free and sourced Maxwell equations remain
smooth-field postulates: point or sheet sources, distribution-valued products,
material excitation laws, and a global potential are outside this scope.

This is an equation-based adoption. It does not assume or imply the existence
of a matter action and is not derived from an action principle. The sources give
formulations in their own conventions; they motivate comparison but do not
establish a physical law or a solution-existence theorem.

post-emg-selected-matter-action.physical_scope: One actually selected smooth classical matter functional with compact variations in a fixed connection sector. Its Hilbert tensor and current are defined by the stated first-variation convention. No existence claim is made for arbitrary matter, and no measured matter model or coupled PDE solution is asserted.

post-emg-selected-matter-action:
## Postulate

For the action-based Einstein–Maxwell branch, choose one actual smooth matter
configuration space $\mathcal C$ on the spacetime and bundle sector of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], and a real differentiable functional
$S_m[g,A,\Psi]$ on its declared domain, where $\Psi\in\mathcal C$ and $A$ is a
connection on the fixed smooth bundle. The field class, transition data and
compact variation class must be specified for the chosen matter model. The
functional is required to be invariant under compactly supported gauge
transformations and orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms, with the
connection and matter fields transported together.

Adopt matter-field stationarity as part of this selected model:
$\delta_\Psi S_m=0$ for every admissible compactly supported matter variation.
For compactly supported inverse-metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$ and
fixed-sector compact connection variations $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$, require the
remaining first variation to have the form

$$\delta S_m=-\frac1{2c}\int_M T^m_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g +\frac1c\int_M j^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, the Hilbert
stress-energy tensor in the convention of
[[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]], and $j$ is a smooth vector current.
The normalization, connection variation, and invariance hypotheses are the
formulation interface used by [[lem-emg-matter-noether-exchange]]; that
conditional mathematical result does not assert that such an action exists
for arbitrary proposed matter.

This postulate selects a differentiable action branch and its variation
conventions. It does not determine a unique action, assert a local or global
solution of its Euler–Lagrange equations, extend the model to singular sources,
or establish empirical validity. The separate equation-based model does not
depend on this action assumption.

post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action.physical_scope: A separately adopted interior variational formulation for smooth fields in a fixed bundle sector and one selected matter action. Only compactly supported variations, or variations vanishing near a physical boundary, are used. Boundary variational principles, singular self-fields, existence or uniqueness of coupled solutions, and empirical validity are not asserted.

post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action:
## Postulate

Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, curvature
convention and SI constants of [[def-emg-geometry-units]] and
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $F$ be the curvature two-form of a smooth
connection in one fixed bundle sector. Choose the actual matter functional
$S_m$ of [[post-emg-selected-matter-action]]. For configurations where the
action is finite, or for compactly supported action differences on a
noncompact manifold, adopt

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}[g,A,\Psi] =\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g -\frac1{4\mu_0c}\int_M F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g +S_m[g,A,\Psi].$$

Adopt that a configuration is dynamically admissible in this branch exactly
when the first variation of this total action vanishes independently for
every smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse-metric variation, every
smooth compactly supported fixed-sector connection one-form variation, and
every admissible compactly supported matter-field variation. If $M$ has a
physical boundary, only variations vanishing on a neighbourhood of that
boundary are included. This makes no claim about a Gibbons–Hawking–York or
other boundary action.

The earlier postulate [[post-em-stationary-action-model]] concerns its stated
flat electromagnetic and prescribed-potential particle sectors. It supplies
no unified matter–gravity action or coupled-solution theorem; the functional
above is an additional, explicitly adopted model. An equation-based
Einstein–Maxwell formulation is a separate alternative, not a premise of this
action branch.

All displayed coefficients are model parameters with the units and
interpretations in [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Compact support is essential:
the Einstein–Hilbert and Maxwell integrations by parts have boundary terms in
general. The postulate asserts neither that its stationary configurations exist
nor that the action describes nature.

pthm-emg-action-field-equations.physical_scope: Conditional equivalence between compact interior stationarity of the adopted smooth fixed-sector action and its metric, connection, and selected matter Euler–Lagrange equations. It asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity improvement, empirical validity, or boundary variational principle.

pthm-emg-action-field-equations:
## Statement

Let $(M,g)$, the fixed smooth connection sector, the constants $c,G_N,\mu_0>0$,
constant $\Lambda$, and the selected matter functional $S_m$ be exactly those
of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]]. Write $F$ for the connection curvature,
$j$ and $T^m$ for the current and Hilbert tensor in the selected matter
variation, and

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad \kappa_E:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}.$$

The homogeneous identity $dF=0$ holds because $F$ is the curvature of the
smooth connection in the fixed sector. The adopted configuration is stationary
under every admissible compactly supported metric, connection, and matter
variation if and only if all of the following hold:

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}),\qquad \delta_\Psi S_m[\zeta]=0\ \text{for every admissible compactly supported }\zeta.$$

The last clause is the selected matter model's Euler–Lagrange condition; an
explicit local matter equation cannot be given until $S_m$ is specified.
These are model deductions from the adopted action and smooth compact
variation hypotheses, not evidence that a coupled solution exists or that the
model describes nature.

pthm-emg-total-matter-field-exchange.physical_scope: Local stress exchange on smooth solutions of the adopted vacuum Maxwell system and one selected invariant matter action. The result is conditional on the matter fields being on shell. It asserts no global gravitational energy, Killing charge without symmetry and flux hypotheses, or coupled PDE solution.

pthm-emg-total-matter-field-exchange:
## Statement

Let $U$ be an open subset of a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Let $F$ and $j$ be smooth, and assume
the adopted Maxwell equations $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ of
[[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]]. Let $S_m$ be the selected smooth invariant
matter functional of [[post-emg-selected-matter-action]], and suppose its
matter fields are on shell. Define $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ by the local Maxwell
variation and $T^m$ by the Hilbert variation of $S_m$. Then

$$\nabla_a T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}=-F^{bc}j_c,\qquad \nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c,\qquad \nabla_a(T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}+T_m^{ab})=0.$$

Set $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4>0$ using the SI constants of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]. If, in addition, the pointwise Einstein equation
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})$$
holds with constant $\Lambda$, the contracted Bianchi identity shows that
the total conservation law is its necessary source-compatibility condition.
This local identity is not a universal gravitational energy statement and
does not imply existence of a solution.

def-emg-charged-dust-model.physical_scope: A restricted smooth continuum model with constant mass and charge parameters, positive proper number density, unit-normalized timelike velocity, number continuity, and the adopted Lorentz-force equation. It excludes caustics, singular particles and any coupled PDE existence claim.

def-emg-charged-dust-model:
## Definition

Let $U$ be an open subset of the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold and use the metric, units, and electromagnetic conventions of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]. A restricted smooth charged-dust configuration
consists of constants $m>0$ in kilograms and $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs, a
smooth future-directed vector field $U^a$ with $g_{ab}U^aU^b=-c^2$, and a
smooth scalar field $\nu:U\to(0,\infty)$, the number of dust particles per
unit local rest-space volume in this model. Define the rest-space projector
$h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+U^aU_b/c^2$. The associated four-current and
matter stress tensor are

$$j^a:=q\nu U^a,\qquad T_m^{ab}:=m\nu U^aU^b.$$

Their length-coordinate SI units are $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ and
$[T_m^{ab}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. As the continuum closure of this model,
adopt on the smooth solution domain

$$\nabla_a(\nu U^a)=0,\qquad m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U),$$

where $\nabla_UU^a:=U^b\nabla_bU^a$ and
$g(F^\sharp(v),w)=F(w,v)$, as in the external-charge convention of
[[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. The latter supplies
test-body sign and normalization context only; it proves neither the
continuum number equation nor a continuum or coupled PDE evolution law.

This definition applies only while $\nu,U,F,g$ remain smooth and the
single-velocity dust description is valid. It makes no claim that such
solutions exist globally or avoid caustics, and it does not assign a
distributional stress tensor to point particles.

pthm-emg-charged-dust-balance.physical_scope: A local deduction for smooth charged-dust fields satisfying the independently adopted number-continuity and Lorentz-force equations. It does not construct dust solutions, prove avoidance of caustics, or extend to singular particles.

pthm-emg-charged-dust-balance:
## Statement

For the smooth charged-dust model of [[def-emg-charged-dust-model]], with
constant $m>0$ and $q$, current $j^a=q\nu U^a$, and stress
$T_m^{ab}=m\nu U^aU^b$, every configuration satisfying its adopted closure
obeys

$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c.$$

This is a model deduction from the continuum equations, not a consequence of
the external test-particle theorem and not a claim that a smooth continuum
solution exists.

def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-model.physical_scope: One classical smooth charged complex-scalar matter branch using the stated gauge-covariant functional and SI bookkeeping. It makes no quantum, statistical, material-response, empirical, or coupled-PDE existence claim.

def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-model:
## Definition

On the smooth Lorentzian geometry and SI convention of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], choose a fixed smooth bundle sector and the
classical charged-scalar functional $S_\varphi$ of
[[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]]. A configuration of this model is a
smooth complex scalar section $\varphi$ and the smooth connection and metric
fields in that definition. In the action branch, take this actual functional
as the selected matter action $S_m:=S_\varphi$, with the same fixed-sector
compact variations. The scalar is classical; the dimensionless field
normalization, the positive coefficient $K_\varphi$, the smooth real
potential $V$, and the permitted coupling $\lambda$ are exactly those of
[[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]].

In its circle-bundle branch, $\lambda\kappa_0=k\in\mathbb Z$ for the selected
representation; in the separate trivial real-potential branch, $\lambda$ may
be any real number. No quantum rest-mass identification, material-response
claim, or existence theorem for the coupled equations is part of this
definition.

pthm-emg-charged-scalar-coupling.physical_scope: Conditional equations for one smooth classical charged-scalar functional coupled to the adopted smooth Einstein–Maxwell action. Current and stress balances hold on the scalar matter equation. No quantum interpretation, empirical matter claim, or coupled PDE solution is asserted.

pthm-emg-charged-scalar-coupling:
## Statement

Use the specified model of [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-model]] and the
adopted total action of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]]. Write
$P_a:=D_a\varphi$, $L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2)$ and

$$E_\varphi:=D_aP^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\,\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\varphi}P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b) -\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi.$$

For smooth fields and the compact fixed-sector variations, stationarity of
the selected scalar matter action in every scalar direction is equivalent to
$E_\varphi=0$. Stationarity of the full action in all fields then gives

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab}),$$

with $dF=0$ for the connection curvature. On the scalar matter equation,

$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=F_{ba}j^a.$$

These are conditional field equations and local balance identities for the
specified classical branch. They assert neither existence of a smooth
solution nor empirical or quantum validity.

ex-emg-classical-scalar-background-limit.physical_scope: Exact smooth plane-wave calculations in the specified classical scalar model on a flat background. They distinguish a matter equation solution from a solution of the coupled equations and make no empirical or quantum claim.

cex-emg-flat-nonzero-field-coupling.physical_scope: A smooth exact counterexample showing that a source-free Maxwell solution on a prescribed flat background need not satisfy the coupled action-based Einstein equation. It uses no empirical data or singular field.
